question: Which of the following geographical boundaries defined the trade monopoly granted to the East India Company under the Royal Charter of 1600?
options: From the Cape of Good Hope eastward to the Straits of Magellan
From the Red Sea eastward to the Sea of Japan
From the Mediterranean Sea southward to the Cape of Good Hope
From the Persian Gulf eastward to the Spice Islands
explanation: The Charter of 1600 granted the Company a monopoly to trade with the East Indies, defined geographically as all ports, islands, and places east of the Cape of Good Hope (in Africa) and west of the Straits of Magellan (at the southern tip of South America).

question: Under what condition could the trade monopoly granted by the Charter of 1600 be terminated by the English Crown before the expiry of the 15-year period?
options: If the trade proved to be unprofitable or not beneficial to the realm, with a two-year notice period
If the Company failed to establish a permanent factory in India within the first three years
If the Company lost more than half of its initial fleet to shipwreck or enemy action
If the Company engaged in direct military conflict with other European powers without Crown permission
explanation: The Charter of 1600 contained a provision allowing the Crown to revoke the charter and its privileges at any time during the 15-year term if the trade was found 'not to be profitable to the host or the Crown,' subject to a two-year warning or notice period.
